text.arabic_uthmani: وَمَا لَنَآ أَلَّا نَتَوَكَّلَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ وَقَدْ هَدَىٰنَا سُبُلَنَا ۚ وَلَنَصْبِرَنَّ عَلَىٰ مَآ ءَاذَيْتُمُونَا ۚ وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction carrying the prior messenger speech into this ayah
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the ayah inside the same messenger utterance that preceded it. The opening is not a fresh detached comment; it resumes the boundary-spanning speech and turns the prior command into the messengers' own first-person reasoning.

topics.headline: resumptive speech across the ayah boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins as continued messenger speech, not as a new narrative frame.
topics.reason: The continuation claim coheres with the conjunction analysis and the negated nominal clause beginning at {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}).

topics.headline: from outward command to inner proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the discourse shift from external defense into self-grounded conviction.
topics.reason: The row family is a discourse claim, and the local clause structure supports the movement from prior speech into first-person reasoning.

words.gloss_range: negative-interrogative particle in the construction that denies any reason not to trust
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) does not seek information in a neutral way. In the {{tr:mā lanā allā}} construction it forces the null answer: there is no reason for withholding trust, so the question becomes an emphatic argument for trust.

topics.headline: question-form that asserts no excuse
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the question itself performs the affirmation of trust.
topics.reason: The QAC grammar and attachment support identify the local construction as negative-rhetorical rather than an ordinary information question.

topics.headline: first beat of the ayah argument
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that trust is established as the opening premise before guidance, patience, and the final command unfold.
topics.reason: The structural row coheres with the ayah's sequence from rhetorical question to proof, vow, and imperative.

words.gloss_range: dative/benefactive lām fused with the first-person plural suffix in the rhetorical frame
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) in {{tr:lanā}} fixes the speakers as the party for whom any supposed excuse would have to exist. The dative frame makes the question about their own accountable standpoint, and the attached first-person plural suffix places that standpoint before the rejected non-trust clause.

topics.headline: speaker-position before the blocked action
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar asks what justification could belong to the speakers themselves, then denies it.
topics.reason: The preposition-plus-suffix analysis supports the claim that {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) marks the speakers' stance in the local construction.

topics.headline: compact dative pronoun unit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how one small unit carries both relation and speaker identity before the trust verb appears.
topics.reason: The local form is exactly the lām plus first-person plural suffix unit described by the CRITICAL row.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive particle functioning in the fused negative complement {{tr:allā}}
words.prose: {{ar:أَنْ}} ({{tr:ʾan}}) is present locally through the fused {{tr:allā}} form, where subordination and negation arrive together. That compact complement does not merely say that the messengers trust; it stages non-trust as the impossible alternative inside the rhetorical question.

topics.headline: subordination plus negation in one surface unit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar embeds the rejected refusal before affirming trust.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence identifies the infinitival complement, and QAC marks the particle as the subjunctive element merged with negation.

topics.headline: affirmation strengthened by a blocked alternative
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah strengthens trust by first making non-trust grammatically untenable.
topics.reason: The negative infinitival complement supplies the local structure needed for the foil reading.

words.gloss_range: Form V first-person plural subjunctive: active self-entrustment to God within a rejected non-trust clause
words.root_gloss_range: delegating, entrusting, relying, appointing a wakīl or support; local Form V selects self-entrusting reliance, not every weak-dependence branch
words.prose: {{ar:نَتَوَكَّلَ}} ({{tr:natawakkala}}) makes trust an active collective self-entrustment, not a passive feeling. Its first-person plural prefix puts the messengers inside the verb, its subjunctive mood places non-trust only as a rejected hypothesis, and the {{ar:و ك ل}} ({{tr:w-k-l}}) field lets reliance feel like assigning one's case to God as the trusted support. The same root also opens the ayah's main argument and returns at the close, so the prior command is internalized as the speakers' own reasoning; the doubled consonant sound gives that tawakkul return audible pressure.

topics.headline: collective trust inside a rejected hypothesis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speakers' collective identity and the rejected hypothetical non-trust are both carried by the verb form.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence support a Form V imperfect subjunctive first-person plural parse for {{ar:نَتَوَكَّلَ}} ({{tr:natawakkala}}).

topics.headline: trust as active agency transfer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that tawakkul is framed as chosen self-placement under God's care, not merely inward confidence.
topics.reason: The local Form V with {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) and the V4 delegation/reliance branches support the agency-transfer payoff.

topics.headline: prior command becomes first-person enactment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the root handoff from the command in 14:11 into the messengers' own self-grounded answer in 14:12.
topics.reason: The local repetition of {{ar:و ك ل}} ({{tr:w-k-l}}) and the immediate 14:11 boundary reference support a command-to-enactment arc.

topics.headline: geminated root sound reinforces the frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the audible pressure of the doubled consonant as the tawakkul root returns.
topics.reason: The sound claim is local and modest: it supports the repeated-root perception without creating a separate lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: preposition selecting the support-object of trust
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) makes trust rest upon a governed support rather than take God as a direct object of emotion. It also begins the ayah's threefold preposition chain: support in God, endurance over harm, then the same support fronted at the close.

topics.headline: trust rests upon a governed support
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that reliance is spatially shaped as resting upon God.
topics.reason: The preposition governs {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) as the complement of the trust verb, preserving the support-image payoff.

topics.headline: first link in the threefold preposition chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah moving through the same preposition from divine support to harm and back to exclusive divine support.
topics.reason: The local word table confirms three {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) occurrences with distinct syntactic roles.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name in genitive after the trust-governing preposition
words.root_gloss_range: divine-name field with worship/refuge derivational discussions; local form is the proper name and the definite endpoint of tawakkul

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: supporting local Arabic display referenced in prose

words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) is the definite proper name governed by {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}), so the delegated trust has a named and singular endpoint. The disputed worship/refuge field may color the trust relation as reliance ending where worship and need converge, but the local form remains the proper divine name, not an indefinite deity term. Its recurrence with word 20 frames the ayah's guidance, harm, and patience between two divine-name anchors.

topics.headline: proper name as governed support
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that trust is directed to the definite divine name, not to a vague support.
topics.reason: The genitive proper-noun parse supports a definite endpoint for {{ar:نَتَوَكَّلَ}} ({{tr:natawakkala}}).

topics.headline: derivational coloring without replacing the proper-name sense
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a worship/refuge pressure around the trust endpoint while keeping the local word as the proper divine name.
topics.reason: The derivational dispute can color the endpoint of trust, but QAC and attachment evidence keep {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) as a proper noun in this location.

topics.headline: first divine-name anchor of an inclusio
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the substantive argument begins and ends around the same divine name.
topics.reason: The repeated proper name at words 7 and 20 supports a local framing effect.

words.gloss_range: circumstantial conjunction introducing the completed-guidance proof

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: supporting local Arabic display referenced in prose

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) before {{ar:قَدْ}} ({{tr:qad}}) keeps connection and circumstance together. The guidance clause is added to the argument, but it also functions as the already-existing ground for the trust claim.

topics.headline: guidance as the circumstance that grounds trust
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance is not a loose addition but the circumstantial proof under the trust question.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence licenses {{tr:wa-qad hadānā}} as a circumstantial clause accompanying the trust verb.

topics.headline: coordination retained inside the circumstantial reading
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the proof is both connected to the prior argument and subordinated as its ground.
topics.reason: Nothing in the guardrails requires choosing simple coordination against the stronger circumstantial function.

words.gloss_range: certainty/completion particle before the perfect guidance verb
words.prose: {{ar:قَدْ}} ({{tr:qad}}) makes the guidance clause a verified completed fact. The ayah does not ground trust in hoped-for guidance; it pivots from the rhetorical question into evidence already accomplished by God.

topics.headline: verified guidance as proof
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance is presented as established evidence, not future aspiration.
topics.reason: QAC identifies {{ar:قَدْ}} ({{tr:qad}}) as a certainty/completion particle before a perfect verb.

topics.headline: from question to evidential ground
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exact particle where the speech turns from no-excuse questioning to proof.
topics.reason: The adversarial setting and clause sequence support reading {{ar:قَدْ}} ({{tr:qad}}) as the hinge into proof.

words.gloss_range: perfect active guidance verb with divine subject, first-person plural object, and an explicit route object following
words.root_gloss_range: leading, guiding, orienting, bringing onto a way, gift/offering branches; local sense is completed divine guidance into traversable paths

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: supporting local Arabic display referenced in prose

words.prose: {{ar:هَدَىٰنَا}} ({{tr:hadānā}}) compresses divine agency and messenger reception into one completed verb: He has guided us. With {{ar:سُبُلَنَا}} ({{tr:subulanā}}) following as the path object, guidance becomes directed routing, not abstract encouragement. The wider {{ar:ه د ي}} ({{tr:h-d-y}}) image of leading toward a destination can sharpen that movement, while local grammar keeps the selected sense as God's completed guidance of the speakers into their paths. That completed orientation also precedes the later harm clause and participates in the surah's guidance arc (14:4; 14:21).

topics.headline: completed act received by the speakers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that trust is grounded in a completed divine act directly received by the speakers.
topics.reason: The perfect active verb with a first-person plural object supports the completed-reception payoff.

topics.headline: guidance as directed routing into paths
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that guidance is concrete routing into paths, while other root branches remain only image support.
topics.reason: The two-object frame with {{ar:سُبُلَنَا}} ({{tr:subulanā}}) licenses route-guidance; the offering and destination branches color the image without replacing the local verb sense.

topics.headline: guidance outranks later harm and echoes the surah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine orientation precedes hostile injury and participates in the surah's guidance pattern (14:4; 14:21).
topics.reason: The supplied references support a same-surah guidance arc and a local contrast with the later harm verb.

words.gloss_range: plural path noun with first-person plural possessive suffix, functioning as object of guidance
words.root_gloss_range: path, road, way, open route, and public-access derivatives; local word names the speakers' guided paths

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: supporting local Arabic display referenced in prose

words.prose: {{ar:سُبُلَنَا}} ({{tr:subulanā}}) makes the proof concrete: God guided them into paths, not merely into a mood of confidence. The plural and suffix make the routes multiple and assigned to the speakers, while the {{ar:س ب ل}} ({{tr:s-b-l}}) field keeps them traversable and available. The variant {{ar:سُبْلَنَا}} ({{tr:sublanā}}) changes syllable weight, not the plural path sense. The possessive also creates a live contrast with divine-speech {{tr:subulanā}} in 29:69 and with same-surah path-blocking language (14:3; 14:30).

topics.headline: the speakers' own path object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the guided routes are grammatically object-like, plural, and tied to the speakers.
topics.reason: The word is an explicit object of {{ar:هَدَىٰنَا}} ({{tr:hadānā}}) and carries the first-person plural suffix.

topics.headline: multiple traversable paths with access pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices route plurality and availability while keeping the local sense as paths rather than activating every public-endowment derivative.
topics.reason: The plural path noun supports traversable routes; V4 access derivatives add coloring but do not replace the local path sense.

topics.headline: phonetic variant without semantic shift
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a recitational pressure point where the middle vowel may lighten without changing the grammar.
topics.reason: The variant is useful as apparatus but local interpretation remains the plural possessive path noun.

topics.headline: possessive reversal and same-surah path contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices how the speakers' 'our paths' answers divine 'Our ways' in 29:69 and stands against path-blocking in 14:3 and 14:30.
topics.reason: The cited parallels supply concrete references and do not override the local possession reading.

words.gloss_range: connector introducing the emphatic endurance vow after the proof clause
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) moves the speech from completed guidance into a performative vow. It does not break the argument; it coordinates endurance as the practical consequence of trust grounded in guidance.

topics.headline: proof turns into sworn endurance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that patience follows as enacted commitment, not as an unrelated virtue.
topics.reason: The following emphatic verb form supports reading the conjunction as a pivot from proof into vow.

words.gloss_range: oath/emphasis lām prefixed to the endurance verb before heavy nūn
words.prose: {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) is the oath/emphasis prefix that makes the coming endurance verb solemn before it is even complete. With the heavy final nūn, it compresses the force of an oath into the verbal complex itself, so the pressure is morphological and fitted to a resisted claim.

topics.headline: oath force prefixed into the vow
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the vow is grammatically sworn, not merely predicted.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as oath/emphasis lām, and the following energetic nūn confirms the emphatic construction.

topics.headline: emphasis inside the pronounced verb complex
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the pressure is morphological, suited to an opposed speech setting.
topics.reason: The prefix is locally bound to the endurance verb and works with the later heavy nūn.

words.gloss_range: first-person plural imperfect endurance verb with heavy energetic nūn in an oath frame
words.root_gloss_range: patience, endurance, restraint, and physical binding/confining imagery; local sense is sworn endurance under inflicted harm

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: supporting local Arabic display referenced in prose

words.prose: {{ar:نَصْبِرَنَّ}} ({{tr:naṣbiranna}}) is not generalized stoicism. With {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) it directs endurance onto what the opponents inflict, and with the lām plus heavy nūn it projects a sworn future commitment. The {{ar:ص ب ر}} ({{tr:ṣ-b-r}}) binding image makes that patience feel like self-restraint under pressure: trust has become an operational posture against harm. The heavy final nūn also seals the vow acoustically.

topics.headline: patience directed onto the harm object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that patience is aimed at specific inflicted harm, not left as a free-floating trait.
topics.reason: The local frame has {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) governing the relative clause of harm after the endurance verb.

topics.headline: binding root plus emphatic future vow
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices endurance as sworn self-binding under pressure, while the local form remains Form I rather than a specialized reflexive form.
topics.reason: The root image and heavy nūn support self-restraint and emphatic future commitment; the Form VIII comparison is kept as contrast only.

topics.headline: trust becomes operational patience
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah moving from reliance on God into the endurance that reliance enables (14:5; 14:21).
topics.reason: The local sequence and same-surah references support a trust-to-patience movement without inventing a new lexical sense.

topics.headline: heavy final nūn seals the vow
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sound of the vow closing with emphatic weight.
topics.reason: The sound payoff follows directly from the heavy energetic nūn on the local form.

words.gloss_range: preposition governing the relative object of endurance
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) turns the harm clause into the surface borne by patience. In the ayah's larger pattern, the same preposition moves from support in God to resistance over harm, then back to fronted exclusive support in God.

topics.headline: harm as the object borne by patience
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that harm is grammatically positioned as what endurance stands over or against.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) as governed by this preposition after the endurance verb.

topics.headline: middle link in the threefold preposition pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices one preposition serving support, adversity, and final restriction across the ayah.
topics.reason: The three local occurrences of {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) are all present and have distinct clause roles.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun introducing the open-ended harm clause governed after patience
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) is relative here, not the earlier rhetorical question particle. It opens the object of patience to whatever the opponents have inflicted, turning the endured matter into a broad category rather than one named grievance.

topics.headline: whatever harm as the object of endurance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second {{tr:mā}} widens endurance to whatever harm is inflicted.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as a relative pronoun, and attachment evidence makes it the governed relative content after {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}).

words.gloss_range: perfect second-person plural causative harm verb with first-person plural object suffix
words.root_gloss_range: annoyance, offense, injury, and caused harm; local Form IV makes the addressees harm-causers and the speakers harmed recipients
words.prose: {{ar:ءَاذَيْتُمُونَا}} ({{tr:ʾādhaytumūnā}}) makes the adversarial relation grammatical: you-plural inflict, we-plural receive. The Form IV causative shape centers caused harm, while the relative clause keeps the harm broad enough to include annoyance, offense, social pressure, and injury. The clause is surrounded by trust in God, so inflicted harm is real but textually subordinated to divine reliance; against the boundary of divine authorization (14:11), injury comes from opponents while authorization belongs to God.

topics.headline: you harm us inside one verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the opponents' agency and the messengers' affectedness are packed into the verb ending.
topics.reason: The local verb carries a second-person plural subject and first-person plural object suffix.

topics.headline: caused harm with wide range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the vow covers a broad range of inflicted harm without narrowing it to a single grievance.
topics.reason: The Form IV verb and the relative construction support caused harm with open scope.

topics.headline: harm enclosed by divine reliance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that human injury remains inside a larger frame of divine authorization and trust.
topics.reason: The local injury clause is framed by trust clauses and the boundary evidence contrasts divine authorization with inflicted harm.

words.gloss_range: connector introducing the concluding imperative while also resuming a fresh closing rule
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the final command as both continuation and resumption. The universal tawakkul rule grows out of the messengers' vow, yet it also stands as its own closing sentence after guidance and endurance have supplied the proof.

topics.headline: specific vow into universal command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the pivot from the messengers' first-person endurance to a general rule for trusters.
topics.reason: The final clause is syntactically a concluding command, while the conjunction keeps it linked to the vow.

topics.headline: the 14:11 command returns with proof supplied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prior third-person trust command reappears after being demonstrated.
topics.reason: The boundary evidence is concrete and coherent with the repeated command form at the close.

words.gloss_range: fronted preposition beginning the emphatic trust object before the final command
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَى}} ({{tr:ʿalā}}) returns at the close before the verb, making the object of trust arrive first. The earlier postverbal support phrase becomes a fronted command phrase, so the final rule restricts reliance to God and reorients the ayah from endured harm back to exclusive support.

topics.headline: fronting restricts the trust command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final command establishes the trust object before naming the act of trust.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the prepositional phrase as fronted before the final jussive command.

topics.headline: support restored after the harm surface
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the repeated preposition returns from harm-bearing to trust-support and escalates from statement to rule.
topics.reason: The local sequence includes postverbal support at word 6, harm-bearing at word 15, and fronted support here.

topics.headline: repetition becomes restrictive closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that recurrence, fronting, and command scope together turn repetition into exclusive closure.
topics.reason: The synthesis row is preserved because its payoff is not merely repetition; it explains how fronting changes the repeated phrase's force.

words.gloss_range: fronted genitive proper divine name establishing the object of the final trust command
words.root_gloss_range: proper divine name with worship/refuge derivational discussions; local closure makes the named endpoint of trust prior to the command
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) appears before the jussive trust verb, so closure priority belongs to the object of trust. The proper name is repeated rather than replaced by a pronoun or title, bookending the ayah's substantive argument with the same divine-name endpoint. The refuge/worship derivational field may color the exclusivity, but the local force is the fronted proper name governing the command.

topics.headline: object of trust before the command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah lands on God before it names the commanded act of trusting.
topics.reason: The fronted prepositional phrase puts {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) before {{ar:يَتَوَكَّلِ}} ({{tr:yatawakkali}}).

topics.headline: derivational coloring under the proper-name endpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the refuge/worship pressure of the endpoint while keeping the local grammar as a proper name in genitive position.
topics.reason: The derivational claim survives as coloring because local evidence does not make {{ar:ٱللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) anything other than the proper divine name.

topics.headline: second occurrence becomes the terminal anchor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second divine-name occurrence turns the speakers' trust into a rule for trusters.
topics.reason: The repeated proper name is now inside a fronted command frame paired with the final {{ar:و ك ل}} ({{tr:w-k-l}}) verb.

topics.headline: divine name bookends the argument
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices guidance, harm, and endurance enclosed between the two divine-name anchors.
topics.reason: The same proper name appears at word 7 and word 20, framing the ayah's main movement.

words.gloss_range: consequence/result connector bound into the final command complex
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the final imperative the uptake of the preceding proof and vow. Bound to the command complex, it carries the fronted object into the jussive verb so the closing rule is consequence, not an isolated maxim.

topics.headline: imperative as consequence of the argument
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final command follows from guidance, trust, and endurance.
topics.reason: QAC marks the particle as consequence/result, and the command clause follows the proof-vow sequence.

topics.headline: consequence fused to the command unit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the command arriving as one closing unit with the fronted object and verb.
topics.reason: The particle is locally prefixed to the jussive-command complex and follows the fronted trust object.

words.gloss_range: lām al-amr making the following imperfect verb a third-person jussive command
words.prose: {{ar:لْ}} ({{tr:l}}) is command-lām. It makes the following imperfect jussive and turns trust into a rule addressed through the third person: not a direct second-person 'trust,' but 'let whoever is a truster trust.'

topics.headline: lām al-amr universalizes the command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the command widening beyond the immediate opponents to the class named at the end.
topics.reason: QAC identifies this as lām al-amr governing the following jussive verb.

topics.headline: command force as a bound prefix
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar performs the command rather than merely describing trusters.
topics.reason: The command particle binds to the imperfect and changes its mood in the local command complex.

words.gloss_range: Form V third-person masculine singular jussive trust verb commanded by lām al-amr
words.root_gloss_range: delegating, entrusting, relying, assigning care or sufficiency; local command selects self-entrusting reliance upon the fronted divine object

words.prose: {{ar:يَتَوَكَّلِ}} ({{tr:yatawakkali}}) turns the earlier first-person self-entrustment into a jussive command. The verb is singular before the plural subject by normal verb-first agreement, so the apparent 'let him trust' resolves into the following class of trusters. Its Form V semantics keep tawakkul as commanded agency-delegation upon the fronted divine name, and the root sequence moves from possible action to command to identity. The variant {{ar:فَلِيَتَوَكَّلِ}} ({{tr:fa-li-yatawakkali}}) makes the command-lām easier to hear, but it does not change the local command sense.

topics.headline: trust as a jussive command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that trust is commanded as enacted self-entrustment, not described as a feeling.
topics.reason: The verb is jussive under command-lām and keeps the local {{ar:و ك ل}} ({{tr:w-k-l}}) reliance semantics.

topics.headline: singular verb resolves into the plural subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices why the singular jussive can command the plural truster class that follows.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence identifies the following active participle plural as the subject of this verb.

topics.headline: from first-person trust to universal command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's local {{ar:و ك ل}} ({{tr:w-k-l}}) arc from the speakers' trust to a rule and finally to identity.
topics.reason: The same root appears at words 5, 23, and 24 with mood and person shifts that support the arc.

topics.headline: variant makes command-lām audible
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a recitational variant that exposes the command particle without changing the governing parse.
topics.reason: The vowel variant is apparatus-level here; canonical local grammar remains lām al-amr plus jussive verb.

words.gloss_range: definite Form V active participle masculine plural, nominative subject of the final command
words.root_gloss_range: entrusting, relying, delegating agency, and being characterized by tawakkul; local form names the countable class whose identity is enacted by trusting
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ}} ({{tr:al-mutawakkilūna}}) names the subject class of the command. The definite active participle turns tawakkul into a durable identity, and the apparent tautology is the point: those defined as trusters are commanded to enact the trust that defines them, upon God. As the final word, it closes the root arc from first-person trust to jussive command to identity-class. The doubled consonant reinforces the audible return, and the supplied profile marks this active-participle class-name as distributionally rare.

topics.headline: active participle names the truster class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closing subject is a definite class characterized by ongoing tawakkul.
topics.reason: The word is a definite Form V active participle plural and the explicit subject of {{ar:يَتَوَكَّلِ}} ({{tr:yatawakkali}}).

topics.headline: trusters are commanded to trust
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the closing tautology defines trusters by the action they must perform.
topics.reason: The subject and verb share the {{ar:و ك ل}} ({{tr:w-k-l}}) family, creating a local definitional predication.

topics.headline: messenger stance becomes universal identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final expansion from the messengers' 'we' to the general class of trusters.
topics.reason: The final word closes the local root and person arc from first-person plural through third-person command into a plural class.

topics.headline: marked final class-name
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final class-name as both audibly reinforced and distributionally marked.
topics.reason: The active participle is locally final and low-occurrence in the supplied profile; the sound claim is kept as support for closure, not a separate sense.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The three w-k-l forms at words 4, 16, and 17 are twice directed toward God, grounded by prior guidance at words 8-9, and paired with pledged patience over harm at words 10-13.
baseline_models.mechanism: The focus partitions agency rather than suspending it: prior guidance supplies a traversable course, entrustment transfers the threatened outcome to a sufficient keeper, and patience restrains panic so the speakers can remain on course while injury presses against their settledness.

activation_trace.role: Handing a matter to another supplies the transfer of outcome while leaving the speakers responsible for their own response.
The one who sufficiently keeps and conducts an assigned matter supplies the competence of the entrusted endpoint.
Gentle indication toward a road or truth makes already-received direction the warrant for present entrustment.
An extended way that can actually be traveled turns guidance into an ongoing course rather than a merely held proposition.
Holding the self back from panic supplies the speakers' active task under pressure.
A disliked injury that prevents ease supplies the pressure against which course-keeping must occur.

changed_reading.before: The speakers simply say that they should trust God and tolerate mistreatment.
changed_reading.after: They reason from an already traveled history of guidance: outcomes are handed to the competent keeper, while their retained work is disciplined movement through injury.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The repeated w-k-l cluster is repeatedly given the same directed endpoint, God, rather than being left as undirected dependence among the threatened group.
baseline_models.mechanism: The root inventory carries both constructive entrustment and a failed pattern in which people lean on one another until the matter is lost. Repetition plus the explicit endpoint concentrates reliance and blocks an equation of trust with reciprocal duty-shedding or helpless inertia.

activation_trace.role: Reciprocal dependence that lets the matter be lost supplies the negative control against which the directed construction is read.
The incapable person who abandons his affair supplies a second passive shadow that the speakers' pledge of patience resists.
Deliberate dependence supplies the positive relation, with its endpoint fixed by the focus construction.
Sufficient guardianship makes the endpoint capable of receiving the matter without licensing human neglect.

changed_reading.before: Reliance could sound like passive dependence caused by weakness.
changed_reading.after: The verse redirects dependence away from mutual abandonment: all entrust the outcome to one sufficient keeper and therefore can persist in their own assigned stance.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The perfect guidance verb at word 8 governs a plural path noun with a first-person plural possessive at word 9, before the renewed declarations of reliance.
baseline_models.mechanism: Guidance can name direction, manner, and lived course as well as indication, while the plural paths are concrete means of reaching. The completed prior act therefore reads as a gifted plurality of conducted histories that generates present confidence without requiring every speaker's route to be identical.

activation_trace.role: Direction, manner, and course enlarge guidance from information into a way of proceeding.
A gracious gift to one held in affection supplies the received quality of guidance, not a route self-manufactured by the travelers.
Multiple traversable means support reading the plural as lived routes toward an end.
Reliance becomes the present response to routes already received and traveled.

changed_reading.before: God gave the group one abstract piece of religious direction, so they now trust.
changed_reading.after: The group invokes its already-gifted, possibly differentiated courses as experiential evidence for renewed reliance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opening movement out of darkness into illumination and a straight road gives the focus paths a directional field. The later blocking, bending, and straying language makes that field adversarial: patience under harm is now course-preservation against attempted rerouting.

activation_trace.role: Direction toward a road or truth anchors the contextual map back in the focus guidance verb.
A way available for traversal is the focus object whose continuity is at stake.
Passage to the outside supplies a real transition rather than static illumination.
Illumination supplies the newly visible field in which a path can be followed.
A straight road supplies the normative orientation of the opening movement.
Turning and diverting supplies an intentional force acting against travel.
Departure from straightness supplies deformation of the route itself.
Loss of guidance and intended direction supplies the end state that endurance prevents.

structural_cues: 14:1 uses a from-to-to progression, turning revelation into directed movement.
14:3 places active diversion from God's way beside the attempt to make it crooked.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies exit, illumination, straightness, blocking, curvature, and straying; I infer that the focus harm functions partly as attempted rerouting. A live alternative is that the harm is abuse without a specifically cartographic function.

changed_reading.before: The speakers have been shown some paths and separately promise to endure injury.
changed_reading.after: They have been brought into a visible, traversable orientation, and their endurance keeps hostile pressure from blocking or bending that course.

context_deltas.mechanism: The call to remember divine days, the pairing of intense patience with gratitude as a condition for recognizing signs, and the remembered rescue through severe trial turn focus patience into a mnemonic faculty. It keeps prior guidance available as evidence when present harm would make the speakers forget their route.

activation_trace.role: Already-given direction is the past evidence that must remain cognitively available.
Bringing something back after absence supplies the retrieval operation by which past guidance bears on present injury.
Self-restraint under pressure supplies the receptive durability associated with recognizing historical signs.
Recognizing a benefit and its giver makes remembered deliverance evidential rather than merely nostalgic.
Release by separation supplies a concrete precedent of being brought through oppression.
A test that exposes the true condition supplies the severe setting in which remembrance and patience become diagnostic.

structural_cues: 14:5 moves from historical deliverance imagery to remembrance and then names signs for the intensely patient and grateful.
14:6 embeds remembered blessing and rescue inside a catalogue of oppression and trial.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies remembrance, recognized benefit, rescue, trial, and patient receptivity; I infer that these make the focus's completed guidance clause a remembered warrant for current trust. Alternatively, 14:5 may only name an audience capable of seeing signs, not a causal memory process.

changed_reading.before: Patience is sheer duration after guidance has already done its work.
changed_reading.after: Patience keeps the history of guidance and rescue retrievable, so past direction can continue to govern action during fresh harm.

context_deltas.mechanism: The opponents demand an overpowering proof, while the messengers disclaim the ability to produce it except by divine authorization and immediately direct believers to rely on God. The focus then grounds that reliance in guidance already received. Trust marks the boundary between faithful witness and control of validating outcomes; it is not a substitute for evidence but a refusal to manufacture or command it.

activation_trace.role: A compelling proof supplies the demanded object that the speakers cannot place under their own control.
Bestowal without exchange supplies the asymmetry of divine favor behind the messengers' role.
Authorization supplies the explicit limit on the messengers' power to produce the demanded sign.
Reliance follows the admitted limit and supplies the stance taken where permission and outcome remain external.
Prior direction gives the focus reliance a positive warrant rather than leaving it in an evidential vacuum.
Transferring the matter supplies the response to an outcome the messengers may not compel.

structural_cues: 14:10 ends the opponents' speech with a demand for manifest authority.
14:11 answers with human limitation, divine authorization, and the same reliance formula that 14:12 resumes.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a demand, inability, authorization, favor, and immediate reliance; I infer an agency boundary between testimony and controlled proof-production. The alternative is that reliance merely closes the speech without targeting the demand for control.

changed_reading.before: The messengers trust because they cannot answer the challenge.
changed_reading.after: They refuse the challengers' premise that fidelity requires command over proof and outcome: guidance warrants witness, authorization governs signs, and entrusted endurance governs the interval.

context_deltas.mechanism: The threat immediately after the focus offers expulsion or forced return, followed by promised settlement and an opening judgment. This specifies the harm as control of route and residence. Entrustment gives God the destination and resolution, while patience refuses the coerced reverse journey.

activation_trace.role: Constitutional inability to remain in one place supplies an exploratory image of harm as induced unsettledness.
A traversed route is the focus anchor threatened by forced exit and return.
Being made to pass outside supplies the coercive displacement arm of the threat.
Return after departure supplies the demanded reversal of the messengers' current course.
Dwelling in a home supplies a counter-outcome to forced displacement.
Judgment that resolves closure supplies an outcome entrusted beyond the messengers' own coercive power.

structural_cues: 14:13 presents an explicit either-or: leave the land or reverse into the persecutors' community.
14:14-15 answer displacement with settlement and a requested decisive opening.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies expulsion, forced return, settlement, and opening; I infer that the focus harm includes route coercion and that patience means refusing reversal. The alternative is that the focus harm is broader and the later threat only one escalation.

changed_reading.before: The speakers endure unspecified mistreatment while trusting in a general sense.
changed_reading.after: They entrust destination and adjudication to God while refusing to let expulsion or forced return erase the paths on which they have been guided.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later followers ask their powerful leaders to avail them, but the leaders confess that guidance was not theirs to give and that neither panic nor patience now provides an exit. This sharply limits the baseline: patience does not compel rescue. In the focus it preserves fidelity during actionable time because reliance is lodged in God and grounded in guidance, not because endurance itself controls the outcome.

activation_trace.role: A sufficient keeper supplies the endpoint that distinguishes the focus reliance from dependence on incapable leaders.
Lack of strength identifies those who had transferred agency upward to human leaders.
Following behind supplies the failed horizontal dependency structure.
The questioned capacity to suffice exposes whether the entrusted party can actually answer for the matter.
The leaders' conditional treatment of guidance shows that they were not an independent source of direction.
The breaking point of patience supplies one side of the scene's explicit failed contrast.
Self-restraint appears here after the actionable interval, demonstrating that the posture alone is not an exit mechanism.
The absence of any turn away from the situation supplies the stated failure of both reactions to create escape.

structural_cues: 14:21 stages a follower-leader appeal about who can suffice for whom.
Its final equivalence between panic and patience is explicitly bounded by the absence of any exit.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies failed human sufficiency, derivative guidance, equalized panic and patience, and no escape; I infer that patience gains its focus function from endpoint, guidance, and actionable timing rather than intrinsic efficacy. Alternatively, the equivalence may apply only after final judgment and not qualify patience in ordinary life.

changed_reading.before: If the speakers remain patient, patience itself will get them out of harm.
changed_reading.after: Patience is fidelity, not leverage over results; its present value comes from guided action under a sufficient entrusted endpoint before the possibility of response closes.

context_deltas.mechanism: The adversarial speaker later denies coercive authority, reduces his role to a call, identifies the hearers' answer, assigns blame back to them, and denies reciprocal rescue. This prevents reliance from becoming abdication: one may entrust outcome to God while remaining answerable for which call one answers and how one acts under harm.

activation_trace.role: Handing over a matter supplies delegated outcome without erasing the agent who performs the handing over.
Denied power and jurisdiction delimit the false leader's actual causal reach.
A verbal call that inclines a hearer supplies invitation without compulsion.
Answering speech supplies the hearers' owned response in the causal sequence.
Censure for a blameworthy act returns moral ownership to the responders.
The denied ability to answer a rescue cry exposes the failure of reciprocal salvific dependence.

structural_cues: 14:22 explicitly narrows causal authority to call followed by voluntary response.
The mutual rescue denial and redirection of blame keep agency with the responders.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies non-coercive invitation, response, blame, and failed rescue; I infer that the focus entrustment concerns outcome, not surrender of moral response. A live alternative is that 14:22 addresses final accountability without defining every worldly act of reliance.

changed_reading.before: Entrusting the affair might mean that the speakers no longer own their choices.
changed_reading.after: They relinquish control of outcome, not responsibility: trust and patience are precisely the accountable response they choose under a pressure that cannot compel their allegiance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The good-word tree has a fixed base and continuing yield, the bad tree is removed whole and lacks settlement, and God stabilizes believers. These images add a stationary complement to the focus's paths: reliable movement requires an anchored orientation. Patience and reliance are the lived rooting that prevents hostile pressure from making the speakers directionless.

activation_trace.role: Holding the self supplies the focus posture capable of receiving the later stability imagery.
A foundational base supplies the fixed orientation from which continuing action can grow.
Continuance without displacement supplies the good tree's resistance to destabilization.
Removal in one piece from the base supplies the negative image of total loss of orientation.
Stable settlement names what the uprooted counter-image lacks.
Divinely caused strengthening links the botanical contrast to believers sustained in their stance.

structural_cues: 14:24-26 opposes a fixed base and recurring fruit to total uprooting and no settlement.
14:27 transfers the stability vocabulary from the image to believers and firm speech.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies fixed base, uprooting, lack of settlement, and divine strengthening; I infer that the focus patience and reliance enact this rootedness while the paths enact movement. Alternatively, the tree image may concern speech and belief without specifying the mechanics of endurance.

changed_reading.before: Guided paths imply only forward movement through persecution.
changed_reading.after: The movement is possible because the speakers are rooted in a stable entrusted orientation; patience prevents motion from becoming uprooted drift.

context_deltas.mechanism: The subjected ship runs through broad water by divine command, while celestial bodies persist in their course. This materializes the focus relation between guidance, paths, and reliance: creatures move through provided systems and means under an order they do not author. Trust is navigational participation, not waiting without action.

activation_trace.role: Direction and manner anchor the navigation model in the focus guidance.
Traversable means anchor the provided routes in the focus plural.
Directing a thing toward a purpose supplies an enabling order that precedes the travelers' use of it.
A vessel moving in water supplies the concrete carrier through an otherwise unstable medium.
Flowing movement supplies actual progress rather than inert provision.
Expansive water supplies the large, uncontrollable field through which provided means operate.
Persistent exertion supplies continuity of motion within the given order.

structural_cues: 14:32 joins divine subjection, a usable vessel, running, broad water, and divine command in one causal sequence.
14:33 repeats the subjection formula and describes persistent celestial motion.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an ordered vessel, movement, a broad medium, and persistent courses; I infer that the focus reliance is analogous to skilled movement through provided means. The alternative is that these verses only enumerate gifts to prompt gratitude.

changed_reading.before: Reliance means ceasing initiative and waiting for a route to resolve itself.
changed_reading.after: Reliance means moving through routes and instruments already made serviceable, while conceding that their encompassing order and final arrival are not self-authored.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah explicitly separates postponement from inattention and later denies that God will miss the promise made to messengers. Focus patience therefore acquires a temporal logic: continued harm and delayed resolution do not show that the entrusted matter has been dropped.

activation_trace.role: Sufficient keeping supplies the focus premise tested by an interval with no visible resolution.
Self-restraint supplies the human practice that spans the interval.
Inattention that leaves a matter outside awareness supplies the explicitly rejected reading of delay.
Deferral to a later time supplies the real temporal condition without implying abandonment.
A promise failing at its appointed time supplies the second explicitly rejected fear.
A spoken commitment that opens expectation supplies the future object carried through the delay.

structural_cues: 14:47 negates promise-failure specifically in relation to the messengers.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies explicit delay, denied inattention, promise, and denied failure; I infer that this is the temporal content of the focus patience under harm. Alternatively, the later statements may concern punishment and vindication specifically rather than every entrusted outcome.

changed_reading.before: Ongoing injury with no immediate relief could count against the claim that the matter is safely entrusted.
changed_reading.after: Patience inhabits the difference between postponement and neglect: the unseen interval tests reliance but does not itself refute the keeper or the promise.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates a bodily, form-distant branch of h-d-y rather than its ordinary directional branch. It remains anchored in the focus's guidance, traversable paths, and reliance cluster, and it yields a coherent motion mechanism. Downstream prose should present it only as a material analogy for guided dependence, not as the lexical gloss of the focus verb.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus places guidance immediately before plural paths and surrounds both with repeated reliance, allowing dependence to be tested as a mode of movement rather than immobility.

activation_trace.role: A weakened traveler moving while supported on both sides supplies reliance as a gait that still advances.
A road available to be traversed keeps the bodily analogy tied to actual forward course.
Dependence supplies the support relation without requiring the traveler to stop moving.

changed_reading.before: Dependence and movement are opposites: reliance begins when the speakers stop advancing under their own weakness.
changed_reading.after: Reliance can be the supported gait by which weakness continues along a guided path; dependence changes how movement occurs rather than canceling it.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the stone and mountain branches of s-b-r and connects them to a late material image of mountains being displaced. It remains anchored in the focus pledge to practice s-b-r over harm, while 14:46 supplies pressure measured by dislodgement. Render it as an exploratory material model of resistance, not as a claim that patience literally means mountain.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The pledged s-b-r at focus word 10 is placed directly over inflicted harm, making the material durability branches available when the surah later imagines forces capable of moving mountains.

activation_trace.role: Thick stone and stony ground supply a compact image of resistance to wearing and displacement.
A mountain and its central mass enlarge that resistance into a stable body.
Departure from place or condition supplies the threatened displacement against which durability is measured.
A high solid mass supplies the contextual object whose movement marks the pressure's extremity.

changed_reading.before: Patience is only inward emotional calm while injury passes.
changed_reading.after: Patience can be pictured as mountain-like positional resistance: harm tests whether a guided stance can be displaced, not merely whether pain can be felt quietly.

strongest_changes: The demand-permission sequence in 14:10-11 makes reliance an agency boundary: the messengers witness and endure without claiming control over proof or outcome.
The failed dependencies in 14:21-22 show that patience is not an escape technology and entrustment is not abdication; endpoint, response, and timing remain decisive.
The expulsion-return threat in 14:13 turns harm into coerced rerouting, while settlement and opening clarify what is entrusted.
The delay and promise statements in 14:42 and 14:47 give patience a temporal logic in which postponement is not neglect.
summary.what_was_special: The focus tightly combines a threefold reliance root, already-completed guidance, plural possessed paths, pledged patience, and inflicted harm. Whole-surah context repeatedly tests that cluster through blocked roads, forced return, failed human sufficiency, rooted versus uprooted stability, provided navigation, and delayed fulfillment, allowing several distinct but anchored mechanisms to coexist.
remaining_uncertainties: The plural possessed paths may denote a shared set of ways rather than differentiated personal histories.
The equivalence of panic and patience in 14:21 occurs after the actionable interval has closed, so its qualification of worldly patience must remain temporally bounded.
The supported-gait and mountain models are branch-backed material analogies, not proposed lexical replacements for the ordinary focus senses.
The focus harm may include speech, social pressure, and physical displacement together; the packet does not force one exclusive form.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Plural paths authorize durable action under harm.** `ه د ي` `B002` supplies intended course, `س ب ل` `B001` extended traversed ways, `ء ذ ي` `B001` unresolved discomfort, and `ص ب ر` `B001` restraint from panic. The plural *subulana* and repeated *tawakkul* frame harm as occurring on already disclosed routes. I infer guidance does not remove friction but makes it bearable as route-cost. The ayah reads as persistence because direction is known, not passive endurance.

2. **Repeated trust is a social relay.** Three occurrences of `و ك ل` activate `B001` (handing over) and, exploratorily, contrast with `B004` (mutual reliance that lets a matter fail). Repetition moves from “we” to the general class of trusters. I infer the second formulation prevents collective reliance from becoming diffusion of responsibility: each actor hands the outcome to God while retaining the journey. This reading depends on contrast with the branch's negative mutual form.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Ayah 14:21 supplied the surprising negative control: patience and panic become equal only after “no turning place” remains, so present patience is valuable because a guided route is still open.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Reliance establishes a division of causal labor.** `و ك ل B001` supplies handing a matter over and `و ك ل B002` reliance; the root occurs three times across the verse's framing. Between those occurrences, the speakers retain two tasks supplied by the packet: walking guided ways and enduring harm. The text gives human movement and patience plus divine handoff; I infer that outcomes, not action, are transferred. `نَتَوَكَّل` therefore reads as active delegation: guided travel and endurance remain human work while result is entrusted.
2. **Plural ways carry one allegiance through different trajectories.** `ه د ي B002` supplies course or intended direction, and `س ب ل B001` extended traversed ways. The plural `سُبُلَنَا` is followed in 14:13 by a demand to return to one inherited `مِلَّة`, then in 14:14 by promised resettlement. I infer that guidance can generate distinct practical routes without surrendering their common source. The phrase reads as divinely oriented trajectories rather than a single socially enforced track.
3. **Collective patience is mutual backing under pressure.** `ص ب ر B001` supplies restraint from panic; `ص ب ر B003` supplies bearing surety or standing with someone. The plural speaker, repeated messenger collective, and shared threat of expulsion in 14:13 supply a corporate structure. I infer that their pledged restraint also makes each stand with the others. `وَلَنَصْبِرَنَّ` can therefore read as solidarity that prevents coercion from isolating its targets, alongside individual endurance.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 14:13-14 supplied the surprise: one side tries to force exit or return, while the divine answer assigns later settlement. That reversal made reliance a division of causal labor and made plural guided ways contrast with a coerced communal track.

findings.text: Güven, sonucu Allah'a bırakırken yöneltilmiş yollarda yürümeyi ve eziyete dayanmayı insanın işi olarak koruyan bir görev paylaşımı kurar.
Çoğul yollar, tek bir ilahî bağlılığın farklı pratik güzergâhlarda sürmesini mümkün kılar ve zorla dayatılan tek toplumsal yola karşı durur.
Birlikte sabretme, baskının kişileri ayırmasını önleyen karşılıklı bir dayanışma işlevi de görür.
Güven sözünün tekrarı, toplu dayanışmanın sorumluluğu dağıtıp işi başarısız bırakmasını önleyen bir karşı örüntü olarak okunabilir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir işi ya da kişiyi başkasına bırakmayı, işi onun yetki ve kararına bağlamayı ve onu kendi adına görevli kılmayı birlikte anlatır. Verilen dal çerçevesi bu devretme işlemini ve bundan doğan temsil ilişkisini doğru biçimde korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal başkasına güvenme durumunu değil, işi açıkça ona devredip onu kendi adına yetkili kılma işlemini merkez alır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, çeşitli çekimli kullanımlarla adlaşmış görev ve temsil biçimlerini ayırır; bunlardan bağımsız, sınırsız bir yalın kök anlamı çıkarmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir işi, kişiyi ya da karar yetkisini başkasına bırakıp o kişiyi kendi adına işi yürütmekle yetkilendirmektir. Kendisine iş bırakılan kişi de bu yetkilendirme uyarınca işi üstlenir.

facets.statement: Bir işin veya kişinin sorumluluğu, yürütülmesi ya da karara bağlanması için başkasına bırakılır.
İşi alan kişi, devreden adına hareket eden yetkili temsilci konumuna gelir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çizgisi, bir işin başkasına devredilmesi ve bu kişinin işi devreden adına yürütmekle yetkili kılınmasıdır; görev adı ile görevi üstlenen kişi aynı ilişkinin farklı yönleridir.

concept_gloss.text: bir işi başkasına devredip onu kendi adına yetkilendirme
concept_gloss.applicability: İşin hem başkasına bırakılmasını hem de o kişinin temsil yetkisi kazanmasını birlikte anlatan genel karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Devretme işlemini ve bundan doğan temsil ilişkisini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir işin yürütülmesi veya karara bağlanması açıkça belirli bir kişiye bırakıldığında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: İşi başkasının yetki ve kararına bırakma yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Yetkilendirilen kişinin devreden adına temsilci oluşunu açıkça söylemez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin belirli bir işi devreden adına yürütme yetkisi kazanması öne çıktığında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Yetkili temsilci oluşturma ve onun devreden adına hareket etme yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: İşin o kişinin kararına bırakılması yönünü geri planda bırakır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, kişinin bir işte kendi yetersizliğini ortaya koyarak başkasına dayanmasını ve onu güvenilir dayanak saymasını anlatır. Verilen dal çerçevesi, gerek Tanrı'ya gerek bir insana yönelen bu güvenip dayanma ilişkisini doğru biçimde karşılar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal birini yetkili temsilci kılmayı değil, kişinin kendi işinde başka bir varlığa dayanıp güvenmesini anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, Tanrı'ya güvenmeyi bildiren kalıpla kişilere dayanmayı bildiren çekimli kullanımları ayrı bağlamlar olarak korur ve bunları yalın köke genellemez.

concept_map.definition: Kişinin bir işte kendi gücünün yetmediğini kabul ederek başka birine dayanması, ona güvenmesi ve işi bakımından onu yeterli görmesidir.

facets.statement: Kişi bir işte kendi yetersizliğini ortaya koyar ve başka birini dayanak edinir.
Dayanak edinilen varlığa güvenilir ve onun işi karşılamaya yeterli olduğu kabul edilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, kişinin kendi yetersizliğini kabul edip işinde başkasına dayanması ve ona güvenmesi üzerinde birleşir; kullanım hem Tanrı'ya hem de insanlara yöneltilebilir.

concept_gloss.text: kendi yetersizliğini kabul edip başkasına dayanarak güvenme
concept_gloss.applicability: Kişinin bir işte kendi gücünü yetersiz görüp başka birini güvenilir ve yeterli dayanak saydığı bütün kullanımlara uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Yetersizlik kabulünü, dayanmayı ve güvenmeyi birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir insanın belirli bir işte başka bir insanı dayanak edindiği olağan bağlamlarda kullanılır.

error_profile.loses: Kişinin kendi yetersizliğini ortaya koyma yönünü açıkça belirtmez.

error_profile.loses: İnsanlara dayanmayı içeren daha genel kullanım alanını dışarıda bırakır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, güçsüz ve etkisiz olduğu için kendi işini başkasına bırakan, ona dayanan ve bu yüzden işini aksatan kişiyi tanımlar. Verilen dal çerçevesi kişi niteliğini, bağımlılık ilişkisini ve işin yürümemesi sonucunu doğru biçimde bir arada tutar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal geçici olarak yardım alan kişiyi değil, güçsüzlüğü ve başkasına bağımlılığı kendi işini yürütmesini engelleyen kişiyi anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, kişi adları ve çekimli bir eylem kullanımından çıkan ortak niteliği korur; bu biçimlerden bağımsız bir yalın kök anlamı varsaymaz.

concept_map.definition: Güçsüz ve etkisiz olduğu için kendi işini başkasına bırakan, sürekli ona dayanan ve bunun sonucunda işini gereğince yürütemeyen kişidir.

facets.statement: Kişi güçsüzdür, etkili davranamaz ve kendi işini başkasına bırakır.
Başkasına sürekli dayanması kendi işinin aksamasına veya boşa çıkmasına yol açar.
Bazı kullanımlarda kişinin ağır ve çeviklikten uzak oluşu da bu niteliğin görünümü sayılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak tanımı, güçsüz ve etkisiz kişinin kendi işini başkasına bırakıp ona dayanmasıdır; işin aksaması bu bağımlılığın sonucu, çevik olmama ise daha dar bir görünümüdür.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, iki kişinin veya bir topluluğun her üyesinin karşılıklı biçimde ötekine dayanmasını açıkça bildirir. Ancak işin bu yüzden boşa çıkacağını kaynak ifadesinin kurucu bir parçası olarak söylemez; bu nedenle dal korunmuş, tanım yalnızca karşılıklı dayanma ilişkisine göre yeniden çerçevelenmiştir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Karşılıklılık zorunludur; işin aksaması olası bir bağlam sonucu olabilir, fakat bu dalın kaynakça doğrulanmış kurucu anlamı değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Anlam yalnızca karşılıklılık bildiren türemiş kullanımlara bağlıdır; yalın bir kök anlamı olarak veya tek yönlü dayanma için genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: İki kişinin ya da bir topluluktaki kişilerin her birinin kendi payına düşen işte karşısındakine dayanması ve karşı tarafın da aynı biçimde ona dayanmasıdır.

facets.statement: Dayanma tek yönlü değildir; ilişkinin iki tarafı da işi bakımından ötekine dayanır.
Aynı karşılıklı ilişki, iki kişiyle sınırlı kalmayıp bir topluluğun bütün üyeleri arasında gerçekleşebilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, iki tarafın da birbirine dayandığı karşılıklı ilişki üzerinde birleşir ve bu ilişkiyi bir topluluğun her üyesinin ötekilere dayanmasına kadar genişletir; işin boşa çıkması ortak iddianın açık bir öğesi değildir.

concept_gloss.text: tarafların işte karşılıklı olarak birbirine dayanması

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi hayvanın sürekli geride kalması veya geride kalmayı istemesi, ancak başka hayvanın yürüyüşüyle yürümesi, koşuda eşine dayanması ya da kötü yürümesi gibi ilişkili hareket bozukluklarını bir araya getirir. Verilen çerçeve, gecikme ve başka hayvana bağımlı hareket çekirdeğini bu çeşitleri silmeden korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal genel yavaşlığı değil, hayvanın geride kalma, kötü yürüme veya hareketini başka hayvanın hareketine bağlama biçimlerini kapsar.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, hayvanla kurulan kalıpları ve kötü yürümeyi bildiren çekimli kullanımı ayrı yüzler olarak korur; hiçbirini sınırsız bir yalın kök anlamına dönüştürmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir hayvanın yürüyüşte sürekli geride kalması, ancak başka bir hayvan hareket edince yürümesi veya koşuda eşine dayanmasıdır; bazı kullanımlarda daha genel biçimde kötü yürümesini de anlatır.

facets.statement: Hayvan öteki hayvanların gerisinde kalır veya geride kalmaya eğilim gösterir.
Hayvan kendi başına ilerlemek yerine başka hayvanın yürüyüşüne ya da koşuda eşine dayanır.
Bir kullanım, bu bağımlı veya gecikmeli hareketi daha genel olarak kötü yürüme diye belirtir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar hayvanın geride kalması, başka hayvanın hareketine veya koşuda eşine dayanması ve kötü yürümesi gibi birbirine bağlı hareket kusurlarını bildirir; bunlar yalnızca sıradan hız düşüklüğüne indirgenmez.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, kendisine iş bırakıldığı için onu üstlenen, yeterli olan, koruyan ve güvence veren görevliyi anlatır. Geçici dal çerçevesindeki deve sahibi anlamı yetkili branch claim içinde bulunmadığından tanımın kurucu parçası yapılmamış, yalnızca ilgili söz biriminin ayrı karşılığında korunmuştur.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, işi üstlenme eylemi ile görevliyi bildiren biçimleri ayırır; ayrı ve tekil deve sahibi karşılığını dalın genel anlamına katmaz.

concept_map.definition: Kendisine bırakılan işi üstlenip yürüten, işi koruyan, onun için yeterli olan ve gerektiğinde güvence veren görevli kişidir.

facets.statement: Kişi, kendisine bırakılan işi üstlenir ve onun yürütülmesinden sorumlu olur.
Görevli, üstlendiği iş için yeterlilik, koruma ve güvence sağlama işlevlerini taşır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çizgisi, kendisine bir iş bırakılan kişinin o işi üstlenip yürütmesi ve iş bakımından yeterli, koruyucu ve güvence veren görevli olmasıdır; tekil deve sahibi karşılığı ortak dal iddiasına dahil değildir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi tapınma eylemini, kişinin kendini tapınmaya vermesini, bir varlığı tapınılır kılmayı ve tapınılan varlığı aynı anlam örgüsü içinde açıkça birleştirir. Geçici dal çerçevesi bu çekirdeği ve ondan türeyen varlık adlarını doğru biçimde temsil eder.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, tapınma eylemi ile bundan türeyen tapınılan veya tapınılır kılınan varlık anlamlarını kapsar; şaşkınlık, yoğun üzüntü ve salt özel ad kullanımları bu sınırın dışındadır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, yalın eylem çekirdeğini türemiş eylem ve varlık adlarından ayırır; türemiş biçimlerin kapsamı yalın eylemin tamamına aktarılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir varlığa tapınma eylemini ve kişinin kendini tapınmaya vermesini anlatır. Türemiş kullanımlarda bir varlığı tapınılır kılmayı, tapınılan varlığı ve tapınma konusu sayılan varlıkları da adlandırır.

facets.statement: Temel eylem, bir varlığa tapınmak ve kişinin kendini bu tapınmaya vermesidir.
Eylemden türeyen varlık anlamı, kendisine tapınılan varlığı veya tapınma konusu sayılan nesneyi gösterir.
Ettirgen kullanım, bir varlığı başkalarınca tapınılır duruma getirme veya öyle sunma işlemini bildirir.
Güneşe kimi topluluklarca tapınılması nedeniyle ona tapınılan varlık anlamındaki bir ad verilmesi, varlık anlamının tarihsel bir örneğidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların ortak çizgisi, tapınmayı anlamın temeli sayar; kişinin tapınmaya yönelmesini, tapınılan varlığı ve tapınılır kılma işlemini bu temelden türetir. Tapınma konusu sayılan yontular ve güneş örneği, varlık anlamının belirli uygulamalarıdır.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه أله وتأله بمعنى عبد وتنسك، والتأليه بمعنى التعبيد، والإله والآلهة والإلاهة لما جعل معبودا.
branches.what_is_not_ar: لا يدخل فيه أله بمعنى تحير، ولا ألهت على فلان بمعنى اشتد جزعي عليه، ولا أسماء المواضع أو الحية أو الهلال إلا من جهة التسمية لا معنى العبادة.
branches.source_phrase_ar: أصل واحد وهو التعبد، فالإله الله تعالى لأنه معبود، وتأله الرجل إذا تعبد، والإلاهة الشمس سميت بذلك لأن قوما كانوا يعبدونها (maqayis)؛ التأله التعبد (ayn)؛ أله بالفتح إلاهة أي عبد عبادة، مألوه أي معبود، الآلهة الأصنام، التأليه التعبيد، التأله التنسك والتعبد (sihah)؛ لا يكون إلاها حتى يكون معبودا، معبوداتهم من الأصنام والأوثان آلهة، الإلاهة الشمس، وإلاهتك وعبادتك (tahdhib)؛ إله اسما لكل معبود، أله فلان يأله الآلهة عبد، فالإله على هذا هو المعبود (mufradat)

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi Yaratıcıya özgü adın kendisini, genel tapınılan-varlık adından türetiliş açıklamasını ve bu özel adla kurulan seslenme ile ant biçimlerini birlikte verir. Geçici çerçeve kullanılabilir, ancak dal yalnızca seslenme ve ant kalıpları değildir; özel adın yalın kullanımı da çekirdekte tutulmalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, özel ad ile bu ada bağlı seslenme, dilek, şaşma ve ant biçimleriyle sınırlıdır; herhangi bir tapınılan varlığı gösteren genel ad anlamına genişletilmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın özel ad, doğrudan seslenme biçimleri ve ant ya da şaşma kalıpları ayrı tutulur; kalıplara özgü işlevler özel adın her kullanımına genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Yaratıcıya özgü adın kendisini ve bu adla kurulan seslenme, dilek, şaşma ve ant biçimlerini kapsar. Bu biçimler doğrudan seslenme, adın ant değeriyle kullanılması veya ses ve parçaların düşürülmesiyle kısaltılma yollarını gösterir.

facets.statement: Dalın merkezinde, Yaratıcıyı başkalarından ayırarak gösteren ve yalnız ona özgü sayılan özel ad bulunur.
Özel adın, tapınılan varlığı bildiren genel addan ses düşmesi ve belirleyici unsur eklenmesiyle oluştuğu açıklanır.
Özel ad, sözün başında ant değeri taşıyarak ardından gelen yapmama bildirimini güçlendirebilir.
Özel adın doğrudan ya da seslenme öğesi yerine geçen bir sonla kullanılması, yakarma ve dilek bildiren seslenme biçimleri kurar.
Ses veya parçaların düşürüldüğü kısalmış biçimler, şaşma ve ant anlatan kalıplarda kullanılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar özel adı Yaratıcıya özgü bir ad olarak tanımlar ve onu tapınılan varlığı gösteren genel adla köken bakımından ilişkilendirir. Aynı adın doğrudan seslenmede, yakarmada, ant bildiriminde ve parçaları düşürülmüş kalıplarda kullanıldığı birlikte gösterilir.

concept_gloss.text: Yaratıcıya özgü ad ile seslenme ve ant biçimleri
concept_gloss.applicability: Özel adın kendisiyle ona bağlı seslenme, dilek ve ant kullanımlarının birlikte açıklanması gereken dal düzeyinde kullanılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü, yanılgının karşıtı olan doğru yönelişi, yolu veya doğruyu incelikle gösterip tanıtmayı, gösterileni benimsemeyi ve ilahi başarı desteğini birlikte kapsar. Verilen dal çerçevesi bu çekirdeği doğru biçimde yansıtır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, sıradan bir armağanı ya da yalnızca yolun kendisini değil, doğru yönü bildirme ve ona yönelme ilişkisini anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak dal anlamı tanımlanır; başka dallardaki armağan, adanmış sunu ve özel kullanım anlamları buraya taşınmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir kimseye yolu, doğruyu ya da benimsenmesi gereken yönü incelikle göstermek ve tanıtmak; gösterilen yönü kabul ederek doğruya ulaşmak, ayrıca bunun ilahi başarı desteğiyle gerçekleşmesidir.

facets.statement: Doğru yönü, yolu veya gerçeği incelikle göstermek, açıklamak ve tanıtmaktır.
Gösterilen doğru yönü isteyerek kabul etme ve ona ulaşma sürecini de kapsar.
Dinsel doğruya yöneltme ve bu yönelişi mümkün kılan ilahi başarı desteği özel bir gerçekleşmedir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar doğru yönü gösterme, yolu tanıtma ve yanılgının karşıtı olan doğruya erişme çekirdeğinde birleşir; anlatım, insanın gösterileni seçip benimsemesini ve ilahi başarı desteğini de içerir. Bir kaynakta itaat ve sakınma da bu anlam alanındaki gerçekleşmeler arasında sayılır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak sözü bir işin yönünü ve amacını, kişinin gidişini, görünür tutumunu ve yöntemini, ayrıca sürmekte olan söz veya işi bırakmamayı birlikte verir. Verilen çerçeve bu çok parçalı fakat bağlantılı kullanımı korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnızca genel bir yaşam tarzı değildir; yön ve amaç bildiren kullanımlarla belirli bir işte veya söylemde kalma kullanımını da içerir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yön, gidiş ve tutum bildiren biçimler ile kalıplaşmış benzerlik ve yineleme kullanımları ayrı yüzler olarak tutulur; özel kullanımlar çıplak kökün tümüne yayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir işin yönü, amacı ve izlenen doğrultusu ile bir kimsenin gidişi, görünür tutumu ve yöntemidir. Belirli anlatımlarda yürütülen söz ya da işten sapmama, başkasının yolunu izleme, ona benzeme veya aynı karşılığı yineleme anlamı kazanır.

facets.statement: Bir işin yönünü, hedefini ve izlenen doğrultusunu bildirir.
Bir kimsenin gidişini, görünür tutumunu ve izlediği yöntemi anlatır.
Sürmekte olan söz veya işi bırakmama ve başkasının izlediği yolu izleme kullanımını içerir.
Özel bir söyleyişte benzerini verme veya aynı işi yeniden yapma anlamı taşır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynak anlatımı yön ve amaç ile kişinin izlediği yol ve görünür tutumu aynı kavramsal alanda toplar; sürmekte olan işten sapmama, başkasının yolunu izleme ve özel bir söyleyişte benzerini ya da tekrarını yapma kullanımları buna bağlıdır.
